arguments.value: DGT hired Dolphin to outsource photo-editing work. DGT would first pay Dolphin $10,000 to test the quality of Dolphin’s editing and the file-transfer bandwidth, paid in two monthly $5,000 installments. If the beta test succeeded, DGT would guarantee either at least $5,000 for each 30-day period over a 90-day period or at least 3,300 photos per 30-day period for 90 days at $1.50 per finished photo, whichever was greater. Dolphin had to finish edited files within 14 days of receiving the originals and meet DGT’s standards. The per-photo price could be renegotiated with written notice. Dolphin could become the exclusive editor for DGT if annual volume reached 50,000 photos. Dolphin was prohibited from copying or reproducing the photos without permission. Dolphin had to keep records and provide annual reports, and information provided under the agreement had to remain confidential. Dolphin agreed to indemnify DGT for claims related to the work, while DGT’s liability was limited and excluded consequential damages. Nevada law governed the agreement, disputes were to be arbitrated in Nevada in English, and either party could terminate only after written notice and time to cure a material breach. The agreement also included force majeure, inspection rights for DGT, and standard boilerplate terms, and it was signed in June 2006.
